source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Corn earworm / fruit borer (ដង្គូវចោះផ្លែពោត, Helicoverpa zea): the larva has five pairs of prolegs. The larval body color can range from green to brownish, and colors can vary widely after molting. Larvae feed particularly on the leaf whorl before it opens, and later feed on the silk within the ear husk and the developing kernels; larva body length ranges from about 35 to 40 mm. Moths lay eggs on the corn silk, taking about 3-4 days to hatch into larvae, which then feed on the silk before boring into the ear itself. After feeding, mature larvae drop to the ground and pupate in the soil, taking about 1 week; adults then emerge from the soil.

Moths of this pest have a wingspan of about 40 mm; females mate soon after emergence and can lay up to about 1,500-2,500 eggs. Eggs hatch within about 2-8 days depending on temperature; larvae feed for about 2-4 weeks depending on conditions. Larvae tend to feed inside the ear near the silk channel, following the silk down into the developing kernels, and can also feed on other host-plant residues in the field. If infestation is severe, this can significantly reduce ear quality and yield.

Prevention and control measures:
- Use resistant/tolerant varieties.
- Plant at an appropriate time.
- Remove weeds present in the field, especially near seed storage areas, and dispose of residue from related host-plant species.
- Collect egg masses and larvae and destroy them by burning.
- Use natural predators, or apply appropriate control measures during silk emergence.
